_about: Seven high-intensity business decisions, each mapped to a persona, an entry point, and the verb-chain that serves it. Coherence is the agent's honest pairwise judgment, given compactly: every pair starts at 'base'; pairs inside an 'align' group strongly agree; 'clash' pairs strongly disagree. The 'expect' is the verdict the honest matrix should produce; 'seam' (for partials) is a clashing pair that MUST surface as a loose trio so the trade-off is never hidden. test_journeys.py builds the matrix and drives the real engine.

journeys.stakes: 9 months runway, two term sheets and a bridge on the table
journeys.prompt: I have a $4M priced seed at a $20M cap, a $2M SAFE bridge, and a strategic round from a platform partner. 9 months of runway. I want to keep control and hit Series A milestones. You decide.
ideas: Take the $2M SAFE bridge, raise A on traction
Strategic round from the platform partner
Hit Series A milestones in 9 months
journeys.reading: Raise via the bridge or the priced round — both keep control and fund the A. Revenue-based financing is the misfit; it runs through every loose trio. The live call it hands back is bridge vs priced, plus whether the strategic partner's distribution is worth the control.

journeys.stakes: $40M ARR, customers need usage billing now, capital discipline mandate
journeys.prompt: We need usage-based metering and billing. Build it, buy the category leader, or partner? Time-to-market and engineering focus matter, and the board wants capital discipline.
ideas: Ship metering in under two quarters
Free the six engineers for the core product
Predictable vendor cost beats build risk
Integrate via their API, no lock-in clause
Board wants capital discipline this year
journeys.reading: Overdetermined buy: every angle (speed, focus, cost, customer pull) points the same way.

journeys.stakes: ordered to cut 15% opex across three teams without stalling the roadmap
journeys.prompt: I have to cut 15% of opex. Options: merge platform and infra, cut the lowest-ROI product line, offshore support. I must protect top ICs, keep delivery velocity, and watch attrition.
ideas: Keep delivery velocity on the roadmap
journeys.reading: You can hit the number, or keep velocity and morale at this depth — not both. The cut locks; protecting ICs and holding velocity are the loose trios. That trade-off is the decision, and it stays with you.

journeys.stakes: re-pricing a SaaS from seats to usage while competitors have already moved
journeys.prompt: We're re-pricing. Pure usage, a hybrid platform-fee-plus-usage, or keep seats with a usage tier? The board wants predictable revenue, sales comp must stay simple, and competitors moved to usage.
ideas: Keep seats, add a usage tier
journeys.reading: Strong lean to the hybrid: it threads predictable revenue, simple comp, and the land-and-expand motion. Pure usage stays loose against predictability; seats stay loose against the market. The hybrid is the pick; the loose trios are the alternatives you're consciously not taking.

journeys.stakes: Series B go/no-go read straight from the data room
journeys.prompt: Diligence read on a Series B. The data room: NRR 128%, top-3 logos at 41% of ARR, Rule-of-40 at 52, founder-led sales with no VP yet, expanding TAM, 78% gross margin, burn multiple 1.4.
ideas: Founder-led sales, no VP Sales yet
journeys.reading: The fundamentals lock — retention, margin, efficiency, Rule-of-40 all back each other. Two risks stay loose: logo concentration against the retention story, and a missing GTM leader against the TAM you'd be underwriting. Price those or get conviction before the IC.

journeys.stakes: whether to extend a VP Eng offer that's over the bar and 15% over band
journeys.prompt: Should we extend the VP Eng offer? She scaled eng 20 to 150 at a comparable-stage company, shipped two platform rewrites on time, references call her a low-ego mentor, the comp ask is 15% over band, we have no eng leadership layer, backchannels are strong, and she can start in four weeks.
ideas: Scaled eng 20 to 150 at comparable stage
Shipped two platform rewrites on time
Comp ask 15% over band, still reasonable
journeys.reading: Clean, overdetermined hire: capability, culture, gap-fit, and timing all line up. Extend the offer.

journeys.stakes: synthesizing client discovery into one staged market-entry recommendation
journeys.prompt: Synthesize the discovery into one recommendation for the client's market-entry sequencing. You take the wheel.
ideas: Land with the wedge product, not the suite
Defer enterprise until SOC2 and references
Price for adoption, not margin, in year one
Hire two AEs and one SE, not a full team
journeys.reading: One coherent staged motion: wedge into mid-market, partner-led, priced for adoption, gated before scale. A confident pick that optimizes to its cheapest equal form.
